order_of_operations_text:
## 2. Order of operations for the LLM

1. Define the deliverable from the request and actual source requirements. Give each requirement a stable ID. Record outputs, accepted meanings, inputs, authority, state, time, quantities, coverage, external effects, failure outcomes and acceptance conditions. Preserve unresolved inputs.
2. Work backwards from every required output. Select the smallest matching family profile. Resolve its required inputs, then recursively select predecessor families or accepted external inputs. Continue until every branch ends at an actual source, a typed human input, an environment binding or a named primitive.
3. Read the full selected family cards, their specific R requirements, universal requirements R02/R03/R29/R30/R32, and relevant proof records. Existing anchors are reuse candidates. Additional proof mappings identify obligations to examine. A mapping alone supplies no implementation.
4. Resolve each selected proof's prerequisites before using its conclusion. Follow every arrow inside its chain in order. A line naming multiple inputs is a join that needs every named input. P numbers identify records; numerical P order is never a universal execution schedule.
5. Build the actual construction graph using O01–O18 and C01–C14. Identify every function by public callable and selected version. Bind exact input/output schemas and meanings. Use qualified existing adapters at incompatible boundaries. A purpose label or unavailable local helper remains a missing implementation.
6. Check every edge against the fourteen-field boundary contract and HG00–HG07. State what the producer guarantees, what the consumer assumes, what the adapter preserves and how errors propagate. No silent conversions of evidence basis, identity, units, authority or completion state are allowed.
7. Resolve the FamilySpec and feature constraints. Generate typed questions for missing choices. Classify configurations as valid, invalid, unresolved or unsupported. Family design, organization configuration, deployment and runtime have distinct binding stages.
8. Derive every applicable leaf, edge, feature, composition, environment and acceptance obligation. Include global properties such as non-overbooking, information-flow limits, conservation, effect uniqueness, deadlock avoidance and progress. A component pass does not discharge these global obligations.
9. Present the complete forward chain from accepted inputs to deliverables. Generate artifacts through the chosen qualified derivation assets. For a factory claim, produce the actual configurator and the actual configured product as separate outputs.
10. Execute the required generated guards and independent checks. HG04 requires actual producer → serialization → reload → adapter → actual consumer. Preserve unknown, timeout, rejection, unsupported, failed and not-run outcomes. Validate actual target effects through their receipt and reconciliation contracts.
11. Evaluate each original requirement against the resulting artifact and evidence. Report structural representation, primitive binding, execution and acceptance separately. A structural fit can remain blocked at implementation or acceptance.
12. Record exact dependency links and the regeneration, invalidation, migration and requalification order after change. Any upstream change that removes support invalidates the affected downstream claims.

For each task return: the required deliverables; selected family profiles; backward dependency derivation; forward function chains with proof/stage IDs; edge contracts and adapters; global obligations and checks; and the unresolved requirements with their exact blocking step. Supply actual outputs when execution is requested and available. Do not attach the research archive to an ordinary deliverable.

During a coverage test, freeze the catalogue. An added family, new semantic rule or newly authored adapter is an extension proposal and cannot be used to score the original catalogue as covering that case. Keep unsupported requirements intact. Failure to find a construction within a search budget means no witness was found within that budget.
execution_contract_text:
## 3. Execution contract

Runtime uses defined functions and data, with zero runtime LLM reasoning. Every meaningful transformation, comparison, resolution, validation, decision and handoff uses a suitable existing public library primitive. Missing primitives or qualified adapters block the affected path. Qualified backend-generated code must remain within that backend's supported derivation contract.

Research the selected public callable in its own project's source or documentation at its pinned version before admitting it. An import succeeding proves installation only. When an independent implementation is needed, search across available ecosystems and examine shared dependencies. A wrapper around the implementation under test cannot be counted as a second engine.

The inherited assurance contract requires generated inputs, independent library expectations or justified invariants, published assertion callables and the standard pytest runner. Hand-authored case functions, expected fixtures, custom comparison helpers and bespoke runners do not qualify under that contract. Historical authored examples below describe intended properties and counterexamples; use generated guards to qualify a current implementation.

Deterministic execution still needs an explicit profile for clocks, ordering, random streams, numerical tolerance and external observations. Statistical, learned and simulated outputs retain their empirical or probabilistic meaning. Defined numerical inference can be a selected capability; runtime language-model reasoning is excluded.

The original P1–P190 chains sometimes name project-local helpers. Their names record historical construction intent and do not establish available public primitives. Apply the attached hardening requirements and research an admissible public replacement where needed. P191–P300 remain theoretical full-chain requirements. P301–P349 retain their specified profiles and open integration gates. No historical run is promoted by this edit.

The later bounded continuation demonstrated a stateless integer SCENARIO factory and native generated-input assertion bindings. Those bounded results do not qualify every family or complete the original whole-chain obligations. The original Ghostwriter-specific P344.S2 remains distinct from the proposed native-assertion alternative.

### HG00–HG07: every function boundary

HG00: Every producer emits a typed envelope with schema name/version, producer and environment versions, payload hash, stable source/record identities, scope, evidence basis, completeness, clock/cutoff contract and validation state. Every consumer validates the exact envelope and payload before work. Changes to schema, identity, units, clock or evidence need a named adapter with a tested contract. A missing adapter blocks the handoff.

HG01: Preserve SOURCE, MENTION, CANDIDATE, OBSERVATION, SCENARIO and RENDERED bases. No implicit promotion of a mention to an event, scenario to actual history, predicted effect to receipt, or discovered process to approved normative process. Validation, authorization and completion are separate gates.

HG02: Whole-input validation precedes effects. Reject unknown required fields, duplicate keys, ambiguous joins, lost rows, unhandled variants, NaN/infinity, stale versions, missing authority and missing source coverage. Retain rejected and unresolved identities. For a stream, define the complete finite event, batch, window revision or transaction being validated before its effect.

HG03: Join by source identity and explicit scope. Never silently join missing keys or merge on display labels. Reconcile inputs into accepted, replayed, rejected and unresolved outputs. Preserve sequence, multiplicity, nulls, typed zero and excluded contributors.

HG04: Execute the actual producer, serialize its output, reload it, call the actual adapter and execute the actual consumer. A substitute fixture checks a local contract only. The integration gate remains INTEGRATION_UNVERIFIED until the actual path passes at its named scope.

HG05: Propagate failed, not-run, unknown, timeout and unsupported states. Keep counterexamples, bounds, termination status and gaps. Sample agreement supports its stated sampled scope; a universal claim needs the corresponding argument.

HG06: Changed upstream meaning invalidates downstream decisions through exact dependencies and expanded-scope reevaluation. Preserve historical outputs. Qualify revised outputs with their new identities and required approvals.

HG07: Keep execution checkpoints cumulative, atomic and append-only; preserve prior failures and evidence. This compact specification contains the definitions and requirements. It does not embed the execution archive or claim that historical files are present.

### Conditional composition proof

Let K specify admitted inputs, allowed output or trace behavior, invariants and permitted failure outcomes. Write Implements(A, K, E) when artifact A in environment E satisfies K under K's assumptions.

Assume (1) each selected leaf implements its contract; (2) each selected composition rule preserves the required observable semantics; and (3) every actual binding and environment discharges that rule's side conditions. Then a finite construction tree implements its derived root contract.

Proof by structural induction: at a leaf, assumption (1) supplies the implementation relation. At an internal node, the induction hypotheses supply the child relations. Assumptions (2) and (3) establish the parent relation. Induction reaches the root.

For sequential composition with adapter T, establish a satisfiable admitted producer domain and the implication that every admitted producer output, transformed through T, satisfies the consumer precondition. T must preserve the specified meaning and other boundary fields. The consumer's contract then establishes the required downstream postcondition. Failure and external-effect behavior must also compose under their declared contracts.

Joins additionally require identity, population and multiplicity conditions. Forks require synchronization and interference conditions. Iteration requires invariants and the chosen termination or convergence argument. Streams and indefinite services require safety and progress over traces. Physical feedback requires timing and model assumptions. Finite syntax alone supplies none of these extra properties.

This proves the conditional construction rule. Applying it requires the actual leaf and rule premises. Semantic completeness of the catalogue and coverage of every domain are separate claims.

O01.name: Acquire and decode
O01.signature: Source locator + acquisition contract -> bounded source bytes or acquisition gap
O01.obligation: Retain source version, media type, byte completeness and acquisition state.

O02.name: Parse and formalize
O02.signature: Source bytes + grammar + accepted mappings -> structured model + unresolved alternatives
O02.obligation: Preserve scope, source spans and accepted semantics; ambiguity remains data.

O03.name: Type and normalize
O03.signature: Values + schema + units + locale -> typed values or discrepancies
O03.obligation: Conversions preserve declared quantities, meanings, identity and loss policy.

O04.name: Resolve identities and references
O04.signature: Records + identity policy -> candidate or accepted links
O04.obligation: Link evidence and adjudication are explicit; every input survives.

O05.name: Select, join, group and aggregate
O05.signature: Collections + query + population contract -> derived collection or measure
O05.obligation: Preserve keys, multiplicity, missing states, predicates and contributor lineage.

O06.name: Traverse dependencies and relations
O06.signature: Typed graph + relation semantics -> closure, paths, components or gaps
O06.obligation: Declare edge meaning, direction, cycle semantics and completeness.

O07.name: Evaluate rules and constraints
O07.signature: Accepted logic + scoped facts -> decision, obligations, conflicts or unknown
O07.obligation: Retain modality, applicability, logic, defaults and all result states.

O08.name: Advance and monitor state
O08.signature: State + event + transition/clock contract -> next state + observations
O08.obligation: Declare ordering, guards, finality, liveness and allowed effects.

O09.name: Calculate quantities and geometry
O09.signature: Typed numeric/spatial operands + model -> computed values or geometric objects
O09.obligation: Conserve exact quantities where required; declare rounding, reference systems and numeric errors.

O10.name: Estimate, infer and fit
O10.signature: Data + statistical/learned model + assumptions -> estimate, model or abstention
O10.obligation: Separate empirical support, uncertainty and applicability from deterministic execution.

O11.name: Search, solve and optimize
O11.signature: Domain + constraints + optional objective -> candidate, solution, bound or unknown
O11.obligation: Retain domain bounds, feasibility, optimality, timeout and infeasibility scope.

O12.name: Simulate dynamics
O12.signature: Model + initial conditions + inputs + numerical policy -> scenario trace
O12.obligation: Control time, random streams, discretization, coupling and empirical validity claims.

O13.name: Select observations and experiments
O13.signature: Question/hypotheses + possible observations + objective -> evidence acquisition plan
O13.obligation: Establish what can be distinguished, at which cost and under which design assumptions.

O14.name: Construct and specialize
O14.signature: Accepted model + configuration + qualified derivation assets -> artifact or generator
O14.obligation: Prove representation and behavior correspondence through construction stages.

O15.name: Render and encode communication
O15.signature: Accepted content/model + presentation contract -> human-facing artifact or delivery intent
O15.obligation: Preserve selected content and qualifiers through layout, interaction and media encoding.

O16.name: Compare and qualify
O16.signature: Claim + named evidence + acceptance contract -> qualified, failed or open claim
O16.obligation: Independent checks execute at the declared scope; no absent evidence is promoted.

O17.name: Persist, dispatch and reconcile
O17.signature: Validated authorized intent + effect contract -> state change + receipt or uncertain effect
O17.obligation: Bind intent, authority, freshness, transaction, retry and external receipt semantics.

O18.name: Diff, invalidate, migrate and repair
O18.signature: Versioned objects + change + dependency graph -> affected set and supported revision
O18.obligation: Preserve historical versions; invalidate all lost support and qualify replacements.

C01.name: Sequential composition
C01.obligation: Every connected output refines its consumer input contract; failures propagate.

C02.name: Keyed join
C02.obligation: Join keys, cardinality, temporal scope and missingness are compatible; unmatched inputs reconcile.

C03.name: Fork and synchronization
C03.obligation: Shared state, branch completion, cancellation and resource interference have explicit semantics.

C04.name: Guarded choice
C04.obligation: Choice has declared overlap, priority and unknown behavior; default never supplies missing authority.

C05.name: Iteration and fixed point
C05.obligation: Bounded loops require a bound; fixed points require convergence or an explicit unresolved outcome; infinite services use a service contract.

C06.name: Partition, map and reduce
C06.obligation: Partition covers the declared population; recombination preserves multiplicity, identity and reduction semantics.

C07.name: Event wait and timeout
C07.obligation: Event identity, clock uncertainty, lateness, cancellation and resume state are explicit.

C08.name: Streaming window and correction
C08.obligation: Each finite window/transaction is validated before its effects; late input and retractions revise dependent outputs.

C09.name: Atomic transaction
C09.obligation: Whole transaction input validates; concurrent execution meets the chosen isolation contract and retry rules.

C10.name: Retry and compensation
C10.obligation: Retries preserve intent identity; compensation follows declared dependencies and never claims impossible reversal.

C11.name: Human evidence boundary
C11.obligation: A person supplies a typed, attributable input; resumption is deterministic and may reject stale or unauthorized input.

C12.name: Feedback and hybrid coupling
C12.obligation: Discrete and continuous dynamics, latency, stability/safety claims and model validity are qualified together.

C13.name: Refinement and substitution
C13.obligation: The replacement preserves the required observable behavior and operational assumptions over a stated domain.

C14.name: Versioned incremental rebuild and replay
C14.obligation: Dependency invalidation, migration, replay and guarded reuse agree with the complete rebuild contract.

boundary_fields.schema: Schema URI/version, dialect, representation, cardinality and null contract
boundary_fields.meaning: Concept, role, modality, qualifiers, units, allowed loss and accepted mapping
boundary_fields.identity: Stable source/record IDs, join keys, tenant, object and purpose scope
boundary_fields.time: Effective/known-at clocks, cutoff, order, timezone, uncertainty and freshness
boundary_fields.basis: SOURCE, MENTION, CANDIDATE, OBSERVATION, SCENARIO or RENDERED
boundary_fields.coverage: Complete/partial/unknown population, exclusions, missing dependencies and acquisition limits
boundary_fields.authority: Principal, resource, action, purpose, delegation, applicable approval and expiry
boundary_fields.state: Pre-state, expected version, permitted transition and concurrency contract
boundary_fields.effects: Read/write/dispatch/actuate classification, intent identity, receipt, retry and compensation
boundary_fields.numeric: Exactness, precision, tolerances, coordinate systems and uncertainty propagation
boundary_fields.resources: Execution limits, deadline, memory, throughput, cancellation and fairness assumptions
boundary_fields.evidence: Claim scope, environment, producer/adapter/consumer versions, hashes and validation state
boundary_fields.change: Dependency IDs, invalidation triggers, supersession, replay and migration policy

familyspec_records.Identity and scope: Stable family ID, version, purpose, supported profiles, vocabulary and source references
familyspec_records.Port declarations: Input/output semantic types, schemas, multiplicities, profile-specific requiredness and complete boundary contracts
familyspec_records.Feature model: Mandatory, optional and alternative features; cardinalities; numeric domains; requires/excludes; binding stages
familyspec_records.Shared semantics: Entities, rules, clocks, quantities, authority, state, effects, unknowns and exception behavior
familyspec_records.Derivation assets: Qualified operation references, composition template, backend targets, transformation contracts and artifact identities
familyspec_records.Question model: Missing-input partition, allowed answers, question dependencies, explanation and unresolved-answer behavior
familyspec_records.Proof model: Per-feature, per-operation, per-edge and global obligations; evidence scope; independence and promotion rules
familyspec_records.Operating envelope: Runtime resources, deployment, data coverage, latency, failure and provider constraints
familyspec_records.Maintenance model: Dependency edges, versioning, extension points, migration, invalidation, regeneration and retirement

guard_generation_text:
## 5. Guard generation and independent acceptance

### GP01

id: GP01
state: SPECIFIED_NOT_EXECUTED
input_generation: Hypothesis6.131.9 strategies generate admissible and adverse inputs. hypothesis-jsonschema0.23.1 is restricted to its supported Draft4/6/7 profile, with common-profile checks for downstream validators.
test_generation: Ghostwriter equivalent/roundtrip style=unittest where native call signatures and domain semantics match. Its output uses public TestCase.assertEqual. No authored case functions or fixtures are introduced.
comparison: Use published NumPy/assertion callables with independent library results or justified output invariants. A fixture literal, same-engine rerun or no-crash result is not silently treated as an independent semantic oracle.
runner: pytest8.3.5 standard runner. Report generated/collected/executed/passed/failed/skipped/error counts, seeds/settings, health-check/rejection behavior and minimized counterexamples.
nonvacuity: Reject st.nothing/TODO strategies, zero tests, all-rejected/all-skipped domains, empty targets and unsatisfiable antecedents as successful evidence.
scope: Per-proof bounded profile, explicit finite/nonfinite/null/time/status handling, exact/tolerant comparison policy and actual producer/reload/adapter/consumer coverage.
unqualified: Cross-language/stateful contract-to-test assembly and incompatible callable adapters require existing qualified generators/bindings; no handwritten test body or runner is supplied.
Important boundary: ordinary JSON Schema validation cannot detect duplicate source keys already discarded by a parser, and type validation alone cannot establish authority, coverage or meaning. The chosen raw parser/schema/model options and any additional public checker must cover those HG02 obligations before runtime admission.

### Oracle independence by computation

I01 | JSON structure | jsonschema / Ajv / Pydantic
  Distinct implementations; accepted common schema profile and matching options required.
I02 | SMT decision | Z3 / cvc5
  Distinct engines; shared semantic encoding and satisfiable antecedent remain obligations.
I03 | Graph/obligation derivation | NetworkX / clingo / SMT
  Distinct algorithms; missing accepted edges/rules remain common-mode failures.
I04 | SHACL Core | pySHACL / Jena
  Distinct Python/Java implementations for a declared Core intersection; pySHACL/RDFLib is a shared dependency pair.
I05 | Relational transforms | pandas / Polars
  Distinct implementations on aligned keys, nulls, ordering, types and cardinality.
I06 | Generated API | OpenAPI Generator / Schemathesis
  Different roles, not independent business engines; real domain operation/state is required.
I07 | Generated UI | JSON Forms / Ajv / Playwright / axe
  JSON Forms uses Ajv; browser readback and independent domain model cover different obligations; axe has incomplete/manual scope.
I08 | Durable workflow | Temporal replay / TLC
  Replay consistency plus separate accepted model; external receipts still required.
I09 | Storage migration | SQLAlchemy / Alembic / PostgreSQL
  Shared stack, not three independent oracles; actual database state and independent reconciliation are needed.
I10 | Program verification | Dafny / Z3
  Dafny uses Boogie/Z3; do not count as independent Z3 confirmation.
I11 | Solid geometry | CadQuery / FreeCAD
  Shared Open CASCADE lineage; exact analytic references support bounded shapes only.
I12 | Spatial topology/reference | Shapely / PROJ wrappers
  GEOS/PROJ wrapper pairs are not independent engines; use separately derived restricted analytic references or qualify another engine.
I13 | Physical simulation | FMPy / alternate FMU runner
  The same FMU may contain the same model/solver; independent model and empirical evidence remain necessary.
I14 | Power analysis | statsmodels / SciPy / R pwr
  SciPy is a statsmodels dependency. R pwr with pinned R stats provides a separate implementation for aligned two-sample t-test profiles.
I15 | ML conversion | scikit-learn / ONNX Runtime
  Distinct selected operator path with native/converter/provider audit; empirical generalization is a separate claim.
I16 | Media | FFmpeg / SoundFile-libsndfile
  Independent admitted PCM path. FFprobe/PyAV share FFmpeg; general compressed codecs are not qualified.
I17 | CRDT and matching | Automerge / matching internal checks
  Convergence/stability checks are invariants; business governance/blocking-pair semantics require independent accepted models.
I18 | Privacy | OpenDP relation / ledger
  Formal mechanism relation and independently reviewed adjacency/accounting; noisy sample agreement does not prove privacy.
I19 | Hybrid proof | KeYmaera X / arithmetic backend
  Record Z3/Mathematica backend; separate model/physical/timing evidence.
I20 | Provider/physical evidence | HTTPX / asyncua / receipts
  Clients are transport tools; actual authoritative state and independent physical observations establish effects.
I21 | Manufacturing interpretation | FreeCAD postprocessor / CAMotics
  CAMotics is a located independent 3-axis simulation candidate. Its automated simulation entry, dialect, discretization and FreeCAD-output binding remain unqualified.
families_preamble: All 38 cards are family contracts with proposed research mappings. Universal requirements R02, R03, R29, R30 and R32 apply to generated family systems alongside each card’s specific requirements. Role names are semantic contract slots; the selected FamilySpec must supply actual schemas, requiredness and cardinalities. Existing anchors identify reusable proof records. Extension mappings identify further proof obligations to select and qualify. Neither list is a runtime schedule.

F01.title: Source formalization and operating-model assembly
F01.product_contract: Compile source-linked actors, objects, modalities, conditions, exceptions, dependencies and meanings into accepted models while retaining unresolved alternatives.
F01.acceptance: Every executable statement has a stable source anchor and accepted meaning; omissions and ambiguity survive as typed gaps.
F01.composition: Feeds decisions, workflows, applications, training and contracts from the same accepted model. External observations enter separately from normative text.

F02.title: Entity identity and relationship registries
F02.product_contract: Maintain scoped identities, relationships, temporal membership and reversible identity decisions.
configurator_questions: Which relationships are directed or transitive?
F02.acceptance: Every record remains accountable; identity candidates, confirmed links and unknown relationships stay distinct after merge, split and historical replay.
F02.composition: Supplies stable subjects for admission, agreements, supply chains, access and historical analysis.

F03.title: Data transformation, migration and synchronization
F03.product_contract: Translate records across representations and versions with declared preservation, loss and reconciliation rules.
F03.acceptance: Accepted, rejected, unchanged and unresolved records reconcile to the source population; required relationships and quantities survive the mapping.
F03.composition: Pairs with connector construction for operated integrations and with application generation for replacement systems.

F04.title: Query, retrieval and knowledge navigation
F04.product_contract: Answer supported queries and expose navigable source relationships under explicit retrieval and population limits.
configurator_questions: Which sources and fields may be read?
What does an empty answer establish?
F04.acceptance: Answers retain exact supporting identities, predicates, exclusions and scope; retrieval ranking never upgrades relevance into truth.
F04.composition: Feeds diagnosis, review packets, decision explanations and change analysis with source-linked records.

F05.title: Rules, policies and scoped decisions
F05.product_contract: Evaluate accepted decision semantics over scoped inputs with explicit applicability, conflicts, missing values and explanations.
configurator_questions: What happens on missing or conflicting evidence?
F05.acceptance: The selected engine preserves the declared rule semantics and returns every required outcome state with its derivation.
F05.composition: Supplies decisions to any lifecycle, transaction, interface or plan without conferring action authority.

F06.title: Authority, access, delegation and information release
F06.product_contract: Determine who may act or receive which information, for what purpose and under which remaining duties.
configurator_questions: Which action and purpose are authorized?
What information can the output reveal?
F06.acceptance: Authority is current and bound to subject, object, action and scope; all output channels obey the release contract.
F06.composition: Gates execution, query, interface generation and shared-system composition. Federated or encrypted computation needs its own qualified backend.

F07.title: Admission, readiness and lifecycle transitions
F07.product_contract: Move subjects through admission, activation, review, suspension and closure only when state-specific requirements hold.
F07.acceptance: No subject reaches an enabled state before all required scoped gates and external readiness receipts hold at the same permitted version.
F07.composition: Composes rules, identity, workflows, transactions and recurring obligations into admission products across industries.

F08.title: Agreements, entitlements and recurring obligations
F08.product_contract: Track version-bound terms, parties, duties, entitlements, notices, renewals and discharge evidence.
configurator_questions: Which executed version binds which parties?
F08.acceptance: Each obligation traces to an applicable term, responsible party, clock and discharge condition; amendment never silently rewrites history.
F08.composition: Drives billing, service delivery, access, asset maintenance and notices. Terms requiring judgment enter as accepted structured inputs.

F09.title: Workflow and case coordination
F09.product_contract: Coordinate permitted tasks, cases, events, waits, reviews and exceptions with durable state.
configurator_questions: How do timeout, cancellation and partial completion behave?
F09.acceptance: Traces satisfy the declared workflow and case semantics; completion, deadlock and progress are checked separately.
F09.composition: Coordinates the runtime products of other families and supplies governed human-input boundaries.

F10.title: Collaborative review and decision records
F10.product_contract: Collect attributable proposals, edits, comments, ballots and approvals into version-bound review outcomes.
configurator_questions: What exact version is being reviewed?
Who is eligible at the decision time?
F10.acceptance: Review outcomes use the correct historical population and artifact version; comments, votes, approval and operational completion remain distinct.
F10.composition: Provides explicit human judgment inputs to formalization, construction, experiments and qualification.

F11.title: Planning, scheduling and qualified assignment
F11.product_contract: Construct feasible task sequences, dates and assignments under prerequisites, calendars, capacity and qualifications.
configurator_questions: Which outcomes and resources are required?
What optimality or feasibility evidence is needed?
F11.acceptance: Every scheduled task has satisfied prerequisites, eligible resources and valid time slots; solver limits and infeasibility remain explicit.
F11.composition: Turns obligations, maintenance, experiments and learning prerequisites into executable work proposals.

F12.title: Routing, packing and network allocation
F12.product_contract: Allocate movement, space and network capacity while preserving flow, location and service constraints.
configurator_questions: Which metric and coordinate system apply?
What capacity and precedence constraints hold?
F12.acceptance: Assignments satisfy the declared geometry, flow balance, capacities and service windows; feasibility and objective quality are separately reported.
F12.composition: Combines spatial models, schedules and material plans. Existing scheduling proofs are foundations; routing and packing need their own chains.

F13.title: Transactions, external effects and reconciliation
F13.product_contract: Execute authorized intents through declared transaction and provider contracts, then reconcile actual effects.
configurator_questions: What is the external effect identity?
How is uncertainty after timeout resolved?
F13.acceptance: Retries preserve intent identity; committed, rejected, unknown and compensated outcomes remain distinct; external state agrees with claimed completion.
F13.composition: Converts verified proposals from other families into observed effects. Exactly-once claims require the full provider contract.

F14.title: Quantitative ledgers, allocation and valuation
F14.product_contract: Maintain conserved quantities and compute balances, accruals, allocations, costs and conditional values with declared units and rounding.
configurator_questions: Which rates and rounding rules apply?
F14.acceptance: Postings and allocations reconcile exactly under the chosen numeric contract; missing inputs never become zero and assumptions stay attached.
F14.composition: Composes with contracts, supply, measurements and transaction receipts to create operational financial and resource products.

F15.title: Material supply and fulfillment
F15.product_contract: Explode requirements, net stock, select supply options and account for material movement from demand through fulfillment.
configurator_questions: Which quantity and unit describe each part?
How are partial deliveries accounted for?
F15.acceptance: Every material requirement and movement has an accounted-for outcome; inventory, packages, receipts and procurement commitments remain consistent.
F15.composition: Combines configuration, geometry, routes, costs and transactions into products that prepare and track physical delivery.

F16.title: Asset maintenance and service reliability
F16.product_contract: Track asset condition and service obligations, construct maintenance work and determine supported return-to-service state.
configurator_questions: What asset version and condition are known?
F16.acceptance: Every due occurrence, inspection result and repair is bound to the right asset and clock; model reliability estimates retain assumptions.
F16.composition: Composes monitoring, diagnosis, inventory, assignment and readiness into a maintained asset lifecycle.

F17.title: Measurement, analytics and reporting
F17.product_contract: Compute defined metrics, comparisons and diagnostic summaries with population and predicate lineage.
F17.acceptance: Every reported measure reproduces from its declared population, units, grouping and missing-data contract.
F17.composition: Supplies measures to forecasting, diagnosis, experiments and planning, with descriptive and causal claims kept separate.

F18.title: Prediction, inference and uncertainty
F18.product_contract: Compute advisory distributions, forecasts, intervals and estimates with explicit applicability and uncertainty.
configurator_questions: What population and assumptions support the model?
Is the claim descriptive, predictive or causal?
F18.acceptance: The evidence supports the stated claim and population; probability, causality, confidence and business authority never collapse into one status.
F18.composition: Feeds governed planning and review routing through explicit policy, with no runtime LLM interpretation.

F19.title: Diagnosis and next-evidence selection
F19.product_contract: Maintain explanations compatible with observations and select discriminating evidence or corrective tests.
configurator_questions: Which tests are authorized and available?
F19.acceptance: Every eliminated explanation and selected test follows from the declared model; an incomplete hypothesis set cannot establish a unique real-world cause.
F19.composition: Combines queries, measurements, plans and actions into adaptive investigation under a fixed selection procedure.

F20.title: Trade-off, portfolio and allocation decisions
F20.product_contract: Select admissible alternatives under declared objectives, trade-offs and allocation mechanisms.
configurator_questions: What constitutes feasible, optimal or stable?
F20.acceptance: Selections satisfy constraints and the reported objective claim; numerical optimality does not establish that stakeholder preferences are correct.
F20.composition: Combines forecasts, causal assumptions, schedules and ledgers. Auction incentives and stable matching are distinct proof profiles.

F21.title: Simulation and digital twins
F21.product_contract: Execute declared dynamic models and compare scenarios while preserving model, parameter and observation provenance.
configurator_questions: Which real system and boundary does the model represent?
How do components exchange time and units?
F21.acceptance: The simulation implements the declared model and numerical coupling contract; scenario output carries its empirical validation limits.
F21.composition: Supplies scenario evidence to planning, design and experiments; operational control requires the separate control and effect contracts.

F22.title: Experiment and measurement campaigns
F22.product_contract: Construct a reproducible plan to acquire observations that can distinguish the intended effects under declared assumptions.
configurator_questions: What stopping and analysis rules are fixed?
F22.acceptance: Design identifiability, confounding, precision and analysis rules support the intended inference; randomization and deviations are recorded.
F22.composition: Composes scheduling, measurement, simulation, analysis and qualification. Existing analytics supply ingredients rather than a complete experiment-design proof.

F23.title: Learning, assessment and qualification paths
F23.product_contract: Construct prerequisite-aware learning and assessment paths, then record which competencies have supporting evidence.
configurator_questions: How does a revised competency invalidate prior qualification?
F23.acceptance: Each claimed capability has applicable assessment evidence; content completion alone never establishes competence or assessment validity.
F23.composition: Supplies qualified-person evidence to assignment and readiness systems and consumes changed operating models.

F24.title: Software application construction and maintenance
F24.product_contract: Generate structured software from accepted behavior models and qualified components with requirements-to-code traceability.
configurator_questions: What behaviors and failure outcomes are specified?
What must remain behaviorally equivalent after change?
F24.acceptance: Generated program behavior refines the accepted model, including error paths, while satisfying declared module, dependency and maintenance rules.
F24.composition: Joins rules, workflows, ledgers and identity with API, interface, deployment and maintenance generators to produce complete applications.

F25.title: API, connector and event-service construction
F25.product_contract: Generate interface implementations, clients and connectors that preserve the accepted service and domain behavior.
configurator_questions: What operation and effect does each endpoint promise?
Which identity and error mappings are exact?
How do event order and duplicates behave?
F25.acceptance: Generated interfaces conform to protocol and domain semantics through real producer-to-consumer execution, including faults and authorization.
F25.composition: Makes existing function-chain results callable and connected; a generated endpoint alone supplies no new business semantics.

F26.title: Infrastructure, deployment and operations configuration
F26.product_contract: Construct deployable environments and operational controls from declared workload, dependency and isolation requirements.
configurator_questions: Which services and permissions are required?
How are builds and dependencies pinned?
What rollout and rollback evidence is required?
F26.acceptance: The deployed environment matches the intended configuration and artifact provenance; health, isolation and recovery claims have measured evidence.
F26.composition: Turns generated applications, connectors and models into operated systems with versioned runtime bindings.

F27.title: Engineering design and manufacturing preparation
F27.product_contract: Construct configurable designs and consistent manufacturing information under geometry, tolerance, material and engineering-model constraints.
configurator_questions: Which physical constraints and acceptance models govern?
What manufacturing and inspection outputs must agree?
F27.acceptance: Geometry, BOM, calculations, instructions and inspection criteria describe the same qualified configuration; physical fitness requires relevant measured evidence.
F27.composition: Composes constraints, materials, simulation, procurement, scheduling and acceptance into products that specify physical things.

F28.title: Spatial and spatiotemporal information products
F28.product_contract: Construct spatial joins, coverage models, geometric transformations and time-dependent spatial analyses with explicit reference systems.
configurator_questions: Which coordinates, units and topology apply?
At what time does a location hold?
F28.acceptance: Spatial operations preserve the specified geometry and reference system within stated error bounds; missing geographic coverage remains visible.
F28.composition: Supplies location evidence to routes, asset operations, environmental calculations, design and monitoring.

F29.title: Document, media and communication construction
F29.product_contract: Generate synchronized documents, graphics, media and messages from accepted content and presentation contracts.
configurator_questions: What transformations or loss are allowed?
Which assets and audience are authorized?
What needs native editability or round-trip fidelity?
F29.acceptance: Rendered outputs preserve the selected content, meaning qualifiers, identities and units; delivery status is supplied by a separate effect receipt.
F29.composition: Provides the human-facing outputs of every family. Open-ended creative choices are accepted content inputs; prescribed media processing is executable.

F30.title: Interactive interfaces and visualization construction
F30.product_contract: Generate usable forms, workspaces and visualizations whose interactions preserve domain state and authority.
configurator_questions: Which actions and states must the interface expose?
How does client validation match server behavior?
What information is visible to each role?
What happens on conflict or disconnection?
F30.acceptance: Interaction, readback, accessibility and error behavior match the accepted contract across supported environments, including concurrent and offline cases.
F30.composition: Turns formal models into usable systems with defined controls, explanations and state transitions.

F31.title: Verification, qualification and assurance
F31.product_contract: Determine which claims have sufficient fresh evidence and produce explainable acceptance, failure or remaining-gap records.
configurator_questions: What exact claim and domain are tested?
Did the required producer, adapter and consumer execute?
What failed, was unsupported or never ran?
F31.acceptance: Every promoted claim is supported at its actual scope; evidence absence, timeout, failure and local-only checks propagate without promotion.
F31.composition: Attaches claim-specific evidence to families, configurations, compositions and generated systems. Formal, empirical and authorized acceptance are separate.

F32.title: Change impact, repair and modernization
F32.product_contract: Determine lost support after change, compute admissible repairs and regenerate affected outputs while preserving history.
variation: Source, schema, authority or resource change
configurator_questions: Which dependencies actually support each output?
What must be reapproved or re-executed?
F32.acceptance: All affected outputs are invalidated or recomputed; unaffected reuse has a dependency witness and no stale authority survives.
F32.composition: Maintains every family and propagates changes through generated configurators into their product instances.

F33.title: Recovery, replay and records lifecycle
F33.product_contract: Reconstruct supported historical or current state and manage record retention, holds and deletion under explicit contracts.
configurator_questions: What deletion scope can be demonstrated?
F33.acceptance: Restored state matches the supported event history and external receipts; retention or erasure claims enumerate replicas and residual evidence obligations.
F33.composition: Provides operational continuity and historical reproducibility for transactions, workflows and generated systems.

F34.title: Streaming detection and governed response
F34.product_contract: Maintain event-time state, detect declared patterns and trigger qualified response intents with explicit lateness and completeness.
configurator_questions: Which detections may trigger which actions?
F34.acceptance: Alerts and derived state respect event identity, time uncertainty and retraction rules; a provisional detector output cannot become a final violation silently.
F34.composition: Composes with diagnosis, workflow and effects to create operational response products; the control family handles physical dynamics.

F35.title: Physical control and embedded automation
F35.product_contract: Generate or configure controllers whose discrete actions and continuous dynamics satisfy a declared operating envelope.
configurator_questions: Which plant model and disturbances are bounded?
How do sensors and actuators correspond to the model?
What happens outside the verified envelope?
F35.acceptance: Model safety and timing properties hold within stated assumptions and are linked to implementation and hardware evidence; simulated behavior alone cannot qualify physical deployment.
F35.composition: Combines simulation, hardware interfaces, monitoring and qualification. This is a distinct proof expansion beyond ordinary business workflows.

F36.title: Analytical model construction and deployment
F36.product_contract: Construct, qualify, package and maintain bounded statistical or learned models with explicit training and inference contracts.
configurator_questions: What labels and features are available at prediction time?
Which objective and evaluation populations apply?
F36.acceptance: Training, evaluation and deployed inference preserve feature, numerical and population contracts; operational claims require appropriate empirical evidence.
F36.composition: Supplies frozen analytical models to prediction and monitoring. This profile permits qualified numerical learning; it does not insert runtime LLM reasoning.

F37.title: Product-family configurator generation
F37.product_contract: Generate a family-specific configurator, its questions, selection rules, derivation plan and required evidence from a formal family definition.
configurator_questions: What varies and what is invariant?
Which missing inputs must be requested?
How does each choice derive components and proof obligations?
F37.acceptance: The generated configurator accepts exactly the supported configurations in its declared domain and emits the specified artifacts and obligations without hidden semantic decisions.
F37.composition: This is the generator-of-generators level. It specializes the construction process for every other family.

F38.title: Assembly of systems from multiple families
F38.product_contract: Assemble independently configured families into one system with joint interfaces, state, authority, resources and acceptance claims.
configurator_questions: Which outputs satisfy which input roles?
Who owns shared state and authority?
How do faults, upgrades and compensation cross boundaries?
F38.acceptance: Every connection satisfies its full handoff contract and the composed system satisfies global invariants beyond local component checks.
F38.composition: Turns qualified families into end-to-end product suites while exposing every missing adapter or emergent proof obligation.

R01.title: Family metamodel and semantic well-formedness
R01.required_claim: A FamilySpec has typed features, valid bindings, unique identities and complete declared derivation and acceptance roles.
R01.required_evidence: Validate actual serialized family specifications, including generated invalid and conflicting variants; compare feature domains with an independent representation.

R02.title: Typed ports and composition contracts
R02.required_claim: For each bound edge, producer guarantees establish consumer assumptions across schema, semantics, identity, time, authority, evidence and effects.
R02.required_evidence: Actual producer -> serialize -> reload -> researched adapter -> actual consumer, with generated schema-compatible semantic failures and explicit missing-adapter outcomes.

R03.title: Derivation of proof obligations
R03.required_claim: Every selected feature, operation and composition rule produces all mandatory proof obligations with stable traceability.
R03.required_evidence: Compare emitted obligations against an independently represented obligation relation over the bounded feature grammar, including interaction-triggered obligations.

R04.title: Valid configurations and diagnostic questions
R04.required_claim: Configuration classification and questions preserve the complete declared finite feature domain, its conflicts and its unresolved choices.
R04.required_evidence: Independent valid-configuration parity; generated inconsistent, partial and boundary configurations; bounded exhaustive domains and separately measured interaction coverage.

R05.title: Generated configurator correspondence
R05.required_claim: A generated configurator accepts exactly the declared supported configurations and emits the correct specialized derivation plan and question flow.
R05.required_evidence: Execute the generator and generated configurator on named FamilySpec bytes; compare with an independent declarative semantics over the same bounded domain.

R06.title: Source-to-operating-model correspondence
R06.required_claim: Accepted source mappings survive into connected entity, rule, workflow, quantitative, interface and requirement views without lost modality or scope.
R06.required_evidence: Source anchors and approved annotation evidence; generated grammar inputs; disagreement ledger and multi-view consistency checks; no independent-engine agreement substituted for semantic acceptance.

R07.title: Behavior model to generated program
R07.required_claim: Generated application observations refine the accepted behavior model, including authorization, state, time, quantities and error outcomes.
R07.required_evidence: Execute emitted code against the source model through independent semantic oracles and generated traces; retain finite abstraction bounds and counterexamples.

R08.title: Architecture and maintainable regeneration
R08.required_claim: Generated modules obey declared dependency, interface and extension rules; regeneration preserves supported extensions and changes only justified behavior.
R08.required_evidence: Compiler/static-analysis and architecture checks; generated feature deltas; rebuild comparison; extension collision and incompatible upgrade cases.

R09.title: Domain model to API, client and service
R09.required_claim: Generated server, schema and client agree on business operations, versions, authorization and error semantics across the supported protocol profile.
R09.required_evidence: Execute generated endpoints and clients with stateful generated sequences and independent domain-state checks, including unknown and unauthorized outcomes.

R10.title: Event and distributed effect semantics
R10.required_claim: Connected event and action chains preserve identity, ordering, retries, receipts and compensation across crashes and provider uncertainty.
R10.required_evidence: Generated duplicate, reordering, partition and crash schedules using qualified fault-injection and state-model primitives; reconcile actual remote receipts.

R11.title: Generated UI, accessibility and model agreement
R11.required_claim: Visible fields, actions, interaction states and readbacks agree with the accepted domain model and accessibility profile.
R11.required_evidence: Real browser interactions against generated artifacts and actual services; accessibility and visual checks; generated role, locale, viewport, offline and conflict variants.

R12.title: Persistence, migrations and concurrency
R12.required_claim: Generated storage and migrations preserve identity, relationships, values and selected isolation invariants under concurrency and rollback.
R12.required_evidence: Actual database engines, serialized migration outputs, independent record reconciliation and generated competing transactions; named dialects and isolation levels.

R13.title: Build, deployment and operational realization
R13.required_claim: Builds and deployments realize the selected configuration with complete declared dependency, resource, isolation and operational contracts.
R13.required_evidence: Actual generated build and deployment artifacts; provenance; measured workloads and faults; environment and dependency hashes; rollout and recovery evidence.

R14.title: Global invariants across family compositions
R14.required_claim: A composition preserves shared global authority, conservation, readiness, concurrency and progress invariants beyond each local contract.
R14.required_evidence: Execute a generated multi-family system with jointly generated states and conflicting demands; formal or independent checks for global properties.

R15.title: Parametric geometry and tolerance
R15.required_claim: Generated geometry satisfies dimensional, topological, clearance and tolerance requirements for the declared design domain.
R15.required_evidence: Independent geometry kernels or qualified geometric oracles, generated boundary designs, named units and tolerances, and artifact round trips.

R16.title: Engineering and measurement-model validity
R16.required_claim: Engineering computations and measured inputs preserve unit, uncertainty, boundary-condition and empirical applicability contracts.
R16.required_evidence: Independent numeric formulations, dimensional checks, convergence/error studies and calibrated physical observations as required by the claim.

R17.title: Design-to-manufacturing correspondence
R17.required_claim: Geometry, BOM, manufacturing instructions, toolpaths and inspection criteria denote the same qualified physical configuration.
R17.required_evidence: Execute actual design exporters and manufacturing consumers; independent part/quantity and geometry reconciliation; measured production evidence for physical claims.

R18.title: Spatial reference and spatiotemporal relations
R18.required_claim: Spatial transforms and predicates preserve declared reference systems, topology, temporal scope and numeric error bounds.
R18.required_evidence: Independent coordinate/geometric engines, generated boundary geometries, antimeridian and unit cases where in scope, and retained uncertainty.

R19.title: Unbounded streams, finality and corrections
R19.required_claim: Windowed computation and response preserve event-time semantics, completeness, retractions and state recovery under the declared source contract.
R19.required_evidence: Generated out-of-order, duplicate and late streams; independent bounded batch comparisons; real checkpoint/restart; finality and watermark evidence.

R20.title: Hybrid dynamics and real-time realization
R20.required_claim: A controller and plant model satisfy declared safety/progress properties and the implementation meets timing, measurement and actuation assumptions.
R20.required_evidence: Formal hybrid-model results, numerical error bounds, code/model correspondence, hardware timing and hardware-in-the-loop evidence within a stated envelope.

R21.title: Experiment design and adaptive evidence
R21.required_claim: An acquisition plan identifies the intended effects or distinctions with declared precision, confounding, randomization and stopping rules.
R21.required_evidence: Independent design-matrix and estimability checks; generated factors/designs and recorded seeds; statistical power/coverage where claimed; measured instrument contracts.

R22.title: Competency, assessment and adaptive learning
R22.required_claim: Learning and assessment selection covers declared competencies and prerequisites, with justified scoring and qualification claims.
R22.required_evidence: Round-trip competency/item exchange; generated prerequisite and assessment states; independent scoring; expert and empirical assessment-validity evidence.

R23.title: Training, inference and model replacement
R23.required_claim: Training, feature construction, model conversion and inference preserve their declared population, numeric and evaluation contracts.
R23.required_evidence: Leakage and split checks; independent conversion/inference comparisons; held-out empirical evidence; numeric tolerances and reproducibility profile; drift and replacement gates.

R24.title: Media and content transformation
R24.required_claim: Generated documents and audiovisual artifacts preserve required content, timing, layout, accessibility and allowed-loss semantics.
R24.required_evidence: Actual export/reload/consumer chains; independently decoded content and timing; layout and accessibility inspection; generated source and format variations.

R25.title: Collaboration, merge and collective decisions
R25.required_claim: Concurrent edits, review scopes and collective decisions preserve attribution, conflicts, quorum and exact reviewed versions.
R25.required_evidence: Generated concurrent histories with independent merge/state semantics; historical membership and version checks; human judgments retained as sourced inputs.

R26.title: Allocation mechanisms and strategic behavior
R26.required_claim: Selected matching, bidding or allocation mechanisms satisfy their declared feasibility, fairness, stability or incentive properties under explicit assumptions.
R26.required_evidence: Independent matching/mechanism checks and generated preferences/bids; proofs over stated participant and valuation domains when incentive claims are made.

R27.title: Retention, erasure and controlled computation
R27.required_claim: Information flow, retention, holds, deletion and privacy-preserving computation satisfy the selected purpose and threat contracts across replicas.
R27.required_evidence: Actual release and lifecycle endpoints; generated joins, aggregates and replica states; privacy accounting; mechanism-specific evidence for any federation or cryptographic computation.

R28.title: Provider, sensor and actuator qualification
R28.required_claim: A real external system implements the required observation, authority, action and receipt contract over its qualified operating envelope.
R28.required_evidence: Pinned provider/hardware specifications; actual authorized observations and bounded effect trials; discrepancy, timeout and unavailable-capability records.

R29.title: Independent assurance and generated guards
R29.required_claim: Every evidence claim follows the inherited library-only, generated-input, independent-oracle and whole-chain requirements at its stated scope.
R29.required_evidence: Pinned primary project documentation; public primitives and assertion callables; generated guards; independently sourced oracles or valid invariants; actual HG04 runs.

R30.title: Change propagation through generators and products
R30.required_claim: A source, family, component or authority change invalidates every dependent configurator and product claim, then qualifies the regenerated result.
R30.required_evidence: Generated changes across all stages; compare incremental results with qualified full rebuild/replay; preserved prior manifests and approvals.

R31.title: Numerical, solver and statistical claim scope
R31.required_claim: Computed claims preserve units, rounding, uncertainty, feasibility and the distinction between bounded evidence and general proof.
R31.required_evidence: Independent libraries or mathematical invariants; generated finite and adverse domains; explicit approximation, timeout, conditioning and statistical coverage states.

R32.title: Source-to-configurator-to-system acceptance
R32.required_claim: Actual source models generate a configurator, which generates a configured system whose executed behavior and evidence correspond to the accepted requirements.
R32.required_evidence: Run all three levels on named serialized bytes: family generator, generated configurator and generated executable system; include change and boundary failures under HG04.
R32.literal_projection_profile: if the formal third Futamura projection is selected as a claim, R05 must additionally identify the interpreter/evaluator, partial evaluator, self-application domain and behavior-preservation relationship. Producing a useful family generator is already a concrete architectural milestone; the literal projection claim needs that extra evidence.

X01.title: SOP to a maintained equipment-booking application
X01.inputs: Accepted booking, qualification and calibration procedures; equipment and staff records; calendar and system contracts.
X01.generated_product: Booking application, generated service and UI, storage/migrations, access configuration, build/deployment plan, requirement traceability and evidence manifest.
X01.emergent_obligations: Concurrent booking requests must preserve non-overlap across UI, API and database. Calibration and qualification must still hold at the contracted reservation/use time. A valid preview cannot commit against a changed equipment version.
X01.change_propagation: Requiring two qualified operators changes the behavior model, reservation constraints, UI fields, service contract, database relations and corresponding proof obligations.

bindings.text: F01 supplies source-bound eligibility and booking behavior to F05 and F24.
F02 supplies equipment and operator identities; F11 supplies resource and time feasibility.
F24 emits the application and storage contract; F25 exposes booking operations; F30 generates the matching user interface.
F26 binds deployment and monitoring; F31 qualifies the resulting instance; F32 maintains the dependency links.

X02.title: Supplier admission through procurement activation
X02.inputs: Supplier procedures, eligibility policy, party records, agreements, approved purchasing-system contract and current authority.
X02.generated_product: Supplier admission portal, evidence queue, approval workflow, procurement connector and recurring review system.
X02.emergent_obligations: Supplier identity, agreement party, approval subject and purchasing-system record must denote the same scoped entity. A provider-created record is one readiness fact among the required gates.
X02.change_propagation: A receiving subsidiary changes the applicable requirements and reusable evidence without erasing the supplier’s other memberships.

bindings.text: F02 resolves the supplier and its scoped relationships.
F05 returns eligibility and outstanding obligations; F08 adds agreement duties.
F09 coordinates evidence and approval work; F06 gates each action.
F13 obtains provider readiness receipts; F07 activates only when all required objects and controls are ready.

X03.title: Configured physical product to delivered and maintained asset
X03.inputs: Customer requirements, approved component catalogue, engineering models, stock, manufacturing process and installation constraints.
X03.generated_product: Configure-to-order design, BOM and cost pack, manufacturing preparation, delivery plan, commissioning and service schedule.
X03.emergent_obligations: Drawings, BOM revisions, toolpaths, inspection limits and delivered serial identity must agree. Resource planning and costs must use the same design version.
X03.change_propagation: A discontinued part invalidates the affected geometry, engineering checks, stock plan, instructions and future maintenance parts list.

bindings.text: F27 emits one configuration’s geometry, material requirements and manufacturing definition.
F21 evaluates design scenarios; F15 nets materials and constructs supply work.
F11 and F12 allocate production and delivery capacity; F13 records actual orders and movements.
F07 uses inspection and commissioning evidence to activate the asset; F16 starts maintenance duties.

X04.title: System replacement with data and operating-model migration
X04.inputs: Source behavior and data contracts, destination requirements, approved mapping, history, interface contracts and cutover constraints.
X04.generated_product: Replacement application, migration and discrepancy pack, cutover plan, compatibility evidence and rollback/recovery plan.
X04.emergent_obligations: Migrated data must support the replacement’s behavioral invariants, including historical decisions and already-issued external effects. Old and new systems cannot both dispatch the same intent during cutover.
X04.change_propagation: A destination schema revision changes mappings, generated storage, connectors and affected historical replay contracts.

bindings.text: F01 supplies accepted behavior; F24 constructs the replacement system.
F03 migrates records with F02 identity reconciliation.
F25 connects remaining systems; F26 supplies rollout and version bindings.
F31 compares supported observable behaviors; F33 preserves replay and recovery.

X05.title: Detection to diagnosis, repair and verified recovery
X05.inputs: Observed events, approved diagnostic hypotheses, repair catalogue, asset identity, runbook, current authority and provider contracts.
X05.generated_product: Incident investigation and response system with a reproducible evidence and repair history.
X05.emergent_obligations: The diagnosis must remain supported by the current evidence. Repeated alerts must not duplicate repairs. A stopped alert alone cannot establish restored service.
X05.change_propagation: A corrected sensor event retracts the affected diagnosis, cancels stale pending work and records any already-completed effect separately.

bindings.text: F34 produces a detection with finality and observation scope.
F04 supplies supporting records; F19 identifies the next discriminating test.
F11 schedules authorized tests and repair work; F09 coordinates dependencies.
F13 executes permitted actions and F31 checks recovery; F33 reconciles replayed state.

X06.title: Research question to laboratory campaign and report
X06.inputs: Research question, factors and ranges, measurement model, instruments, permitted resources and declared analysis.
X06.generated_product: Experiment planner, run orchestration, instrument bindings, analysis and reproducible report.
X06.emergent_obligations: Scheduling changes cannot silently destroy randomization or blocking. Missing runs and instrument changes must alter the supported estimands and uncertainty.
X06.change_propagation: A failed instrument creates a revised measurement contract, affected-run ledger and re-evaluation of which comparisons remain supported.

bindings.text: F22 emits a design and analysis contract; F11 assigns runs and resources.
F25 exposes instrument operations; F13 records actual measurements and failures.
F17 reconciles observations; F18 executes the declared analysis.
F29 publishes source-linked results and F31 qualifies the claims supported by the actual campaign.

X07.title: Procedure revision to qualified workforce coverage
X07.inputs: Accepted procedure delta, competency mappings, learning assets, assessments, workforce and assignment records.
X07.generated_product: Procedure-linked learning, assessment, reassessment and qualified staffing system.
X07.emergent_obligations: The person, competency, procedure version and assessed evidence must agree across learning and access systems. Previous course attendance cannot silently satisfy a revised capability.
X07.change_propagation: A new equipment procedure invalidates only the affected qualification claims and dependent assignments, using explicit mappings.

bindings.text: F32 identifies changed competencies from the F01 operating-model revision.
F23 creates targeted learning and assessment paths.
F11 schedules assessment and work coverage; F30 exposes the learner and assessor views.
F07 accepts new qualification evidence before enabling restricted work.

X08.title: Agreement to usage billing, collection and entitlement
X08.inputs: Accepted agreement terms, account identity, usage events, pricing and tax inputs where applicable, payment interface and entitlement policy.
X08.generated_product: Metering, billing, collection, dispute and entitlement product suite.
X08.emergent_obligations: Usage window, price version, payer and service identity must match. A payment timeout is an unknown effect, and must not cause a second charge or an unjustified suspension.
X08.change_propagation: A backdated meter correction changes the affected ledger and adjustment duties while retaining the original invoice history.

bindings.text: F08 emits version-bound terms and duties; F34 reconciles usage events.
F17 computes billable quantities and F14 generates the charge ledger.
F13 reconciles payment effects.
F05 and F07 update entitlements using the applicable grace, dispute and suspension policy.

X09.title: Spatial observation to field response
X09.inputs: Sensor or inspection observations, coordinates and uncertainty, geographic boundaries, resource availability and response policy.
X09.generated_product: Environmental response, utility fieldwork or geospatial service operations system.
X09.emergent_obligations: Coordinate systems, time windows and uncertainty must agree before dispatch. A route plan cannot imply arrival or resolution.
X09.change_propagation: A corrected boundary or coordinate reference invalidates affected detections, coverage totals and unexecuted dispatch proposals.

bindings.text: F28 resolves spatial and temporal membership; F34 detects supported threshold events.
F19 requests additional observations where location or cause remains uncertain.
F11 and F12 allocate qualified field resources and routes.
F13 records field actions and F17 measures actual outcomes.

X10.title: Model-based controller construction and operation
X10.inputs: Accepted plant and control models, geometry, disturbances, timing requirements, sensor/actuator contract and deployment target.
X10.generated_product: A bounded control-system configuration with generated software, device bindings and explicit deployment evidence requirements.
X10.emergent_obligations: Sensor error, execution time, communication latency and actuator saturation must fit the verified assumptions jointly. The simulation clock cannot stand in for hardware timing.
X10.change_propagation: A changed sampling rate or actuator model requires renewed hybrid, implementation and timing qualification.

bindings.text: F21 supplies model simulation and numerical coupling evidence.
F35 supplies control invariants and the operating envelope.
F24 and F25 generate the bounded controller implementation and hardware bindings.
F26 binds the runtime; F31 joins formal, implementation and hardware evidence; F34 records monitored conditions.

X11.title: One accepted model to synchronized audience outputs
X11.inputs: Accepted content, data, source model, audience access policy, format requirements and review state.
X11.generated_product: A synchronized publishing and review system with native, printable and interactive outputs.
X11.emergent_obligations: Audience filtering must happen before every output and derivative, including notes, attachments, hidden fields and cached views. Review must bind to the actual exported version.
X11.change_propagation: Changing one amount or release permission identifies all affected formats, cached interfaces and prior approvals.

bindings.text: F04 and F17 produce authorized source-linked records and measures.
F06 derives each audience’s allowed view.
F29 generates documents, slides, messages and media; F30 generates matching interactive views.
F10 binds review to each artifact version; F32 invalidates affected outputs on source change.

X12.title: Generator of configurable operating systems
X12.inputs: Family specifications, feature models, qualified capabilities, operating models, target profiles, derivation assets and proof requirements.
X12.generated_product: A reusable factory that generates family configurators and then configured executable systems with evidence and change manifests.
X12.emergent_obligations: Correctness must survive both generation steps and cross-family assembly. Valid local feature choices may still create incompatible shared state, authority or capacity.
X12.change_propagation: A new qualified component changes the available configuration space and downstream generator/product obligations with explicit compatibility and migration evidence.

bindings.text: F37 generates a configurator for each selected family definition.
Each configurator binds organization-specific models and target constraints.
F24, F25, F26 and F30 construct the selected software, service, environment and interface artifacts.
F38 composes the members and derives global obligations; F31 qualifies the resulting system and F32 maintains its derivation lineage.

L01.name: Pydantic

entries.contract: An accepted type and explicit strict/extra policy; validate all records before effects.
Retain aliases, nulls, discriminators and envelope fields; serialize the validated model.

L01.assurance: jsonschema plus Ajv over a declared common schema subset
L01.boundary: Strict JSON and strict Python have different accepted representations; coercions, extra fields and non-finite values need explicit configuration.

L02.name: jsonschema

entries.contract: Pin Draft 2020-12; explicit format checking and reference registry; reject unexpected fields in the contract.

L02.role: JSON Schema validation and schema checking
L02.assurance: Ajv 8.17.1 is a separate implementation; align dialect and format settings
L02.boundary: Schema validation cannot establish source semantics, key uniqueness across objects or authority.

L03.name: Ajv

entries.contract: Import ajv/dist/2020; pin strictness, coercion disabled, defaults disabled, matching formats and reference set.

P191.title: approved source clauses -> controlled syntax tree -> typed rule records
P191.reuses: P1 candidate extraction and source checking; P95 strict field contracts
P191.new_capability: Lark controlled-language compiler with explicit semantic acceptance
P191.contract: Grammar and semantics are versioned separately. require, permit, and forbid are distinct. Boolean connectors have declared precedence. Source-candidate extraction cannot silently approve a mapping.
P191.theoretical_positive_test: For the S01 four-voting-member minimum, an approved count >= 4 expression retains actor, integer threshold, and clause reference. The four-member boundary satisfies the expression; three does not.

P248.title: untrusted structured proposal -> typed verifier and permitted action map -> accepted intent or explicit exception

P248.theoretical_adverse_test: Injected instructions, an unknown activate action, a fabricated citation, an unsupported exception, or a verifier timeout cannot dispatch an effect. Two agreeing solvers based on the same faulty translation are insufficient semantic assurance.
P248.assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for bounded structured actions and claims covered by explicit validators. Open-ended language verification remains outside the certified subset.
P248.public_data_limit: Public samples cannot establish that every future proposal is correctly interpreted or every production action is safe. This assessment does not qualify a runtime agent loop.

P250.theoretical_adverse_test: Replacing one required result with not_run blocks qualification even when a signoff exists. A report that counts an empty target set, uses stale source hashes, or silently drops missing-stage records is rejected.

P251.title: concurrent intakes and identity candidates -> purpose-bound consolidation -> linked request families

P251.theoretical_adverse_test: Change the receiving entity or purpose on one request: automatic consolidation is blocked or separately authorized. A high name-match score alone cannot merge the cases. A reused intake key with different bytes produces a conflict.

The prior member stays unchanged; the new member cannot activate until its three obligations and current approvals are evidenced.

P253.title: direct ownership interests and declared summaries -> exact path accounting -> bounded look-through result

An indirect summary and its components are alternate descriptions of one interest. A threshold is an approved input, never selected from a demonstration jurisdiction.

P253.theoretical_adverse_test: Adding that summary again would produce 7/10 and must fail. A cycle, incompatible voting/economic classes, overlapping duplicate holdings, or missing interest does not produce an asserted exact ownership result. An interval crossing a configured threshold remains unresolved.
P253.assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for exact, bounded look-through arithmetic and declaration consistency. Control classification and policy conclusions require a separate approved rule layer.

P254.title: trust and nominee structures -> typed party roles and unknowns -> role-specific evidence requirements
P254.reuses: P191 typed rules; P194 shape coverage; P202 entity limits; P253 share/control separation
P254.new_capability: BODS role graphs + pySHACL + clingo role-sensitive derivation
P254.contract: One person may hold several roles. A combined role does not create a second person or erase a control duty. Unknown, undisclosed, exempt-from-disclosure, and absent-from-data have different meanings. Representation of legal personality must come from an explicit source.
P254.theoretical_positive_test: An authored person who is both settlor and trustee retains one identity and two role edges. A nominee and nominator remain distinct roles connected through the arrangement. Separate approved role rules create independently traceable evidence requirements.
P254.theoretical_adverse_test: Giving every trust party an equal share or treating a nominee as the beneficial owner solely from the nominee role is rejected. An anonymous beneficiary produces the declared unresolved identity condition, never an invented name or zero obligation.
