P255.title: dated ownership update and periodic review clock -> scoped re-entry -> review episode with retained history
title_roles: dated ownership update and periodic review clock
P255.reuses: P211 bitemporal facts; P212 new-scope impact; P215 review clocks; P241 durable history
P255.new_capability: BODS updates + Temporal review episodes + PROV derivation lineage
P255.contract: A periodic confirmation and a substantive change are distinct events. A changed ownership fact may trigger work before the next periodic date. Whether confirmation resets a clock is a versioned rule input. Earlier review completion remains historical and does not approve new facts.
P255.theoretical_positive_test: An authored no-change confirmation preserves the requirement set. A later qualifying ownership update starts one change-review episode, links to the old episode, and reassesses only the explicitly affected requirements plus new-scope requirements.
P255.theoretical_adverse_test: Replay the same update twice: one episode results. A late-recorded correction cannot change what was known at an earlier cutoff. Moving the periodic date must not suppress a separately due substantive-change trigger.
P255.assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for one lifecycle with explicit review re-entry and preserved decision history.
P255.public_data_limit: The fictional ownership timeline supplies no institution-specific review cadence, materiality trigger, or permission to retain a prior approval.

P256.title: offboarding instruction and dependencies -> controlled deactivation -> closure evidence and outstanding holds
P256.reuses: P216 safety; P221 planning; P243 compensation; P244 stale-state fencing
P256.new_capability: SCIM lifecycle analogue + Unified Planning + Temporal + temporal safety checks
P256.contract: Deleting a technical identity resource does not discharge business obligations. A 404 can mean absent or unavailable under the service's semantics; it needs contextual reconciliation. Retention rules are explicit inputs. Historical evidence is never deleted as a convenience of closing an operational case.
P256.theoretical_positive_test: An authored three-resource offboard operation deactivates two eligible resources, retains one on an explicit hold, and reports partial closure. The case remains incomplete until every required closure condition has matching evidence.
P256.theoretical_adverse_test: One 204 response cannot close all three resources. A resource belonging to another tenant, a stale authorization, an open mandatory dependency, or an active retention hold blocks its prohibited operation.
P256.assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for mechanically controlled offboarding and honest partial completion.
P256.public_data_limit: SCIM examples test identity-resource operations. They do not demonstrate settlement, financial account closure, record-retention law, or the semantics of proprietary downstream systems.

P257.title: configuration operations and provider receipts -> object-level readiness barrier -> qualified activation state
P257.reuses: P199 evidence gates; P207 interfaces; P210 event scope; P242 retries; P244 commit fence
P257.new_capability: OpenAPI contract tests + Schemathesis + Temporal + SHACL readiness barrier
P257.contract: Readiness is a conjunction over the manifest's required operations, plus current authority and evidence. Empty or incomplete manifests cannot pass. Transport success, accepted work, and verified business configuration remain distinct. Readiness may be invalidated by later changes.
P257.theoretical_positive_test: An authored two-operation manifest with exact matching success receipts and current approvals satisfies the modeled barrier. The public SCIM all-failed bulk example yields failed operations despite its enclosing 200 response.
P257.theoretical_adverse_test: A 200 response with one failed operation, a missing second receipt, a wrong-object receipt, or a stale version cannot produce ready status. A configuration change after the assertion invalidates or requires revalidation of that assertion.

P258.title: product and jurisdiction request -> eligibility and duty evaluation -> scoped intake decision
P258.reuses: P192 applicability; P193 contradictions; P198 coverage; P200 resolver; P206 authority
P258.new_capability: Zen/clingo/Z3 parity over separate eligibility, prohibition, and obligation dimensions
P258.contract: Eligibility to request a product, duty to collect evidence, and permission to activate are different predicates. A specific permissive rule does not automatically override a prohibition. Rule precedence must be explicit, scoped, versioned, and approved.
P258.theoretical_positive_test: In an authored model, a qualified client in market A can submit product X, yet activation remains blocked until evidence and approval requirements pass. An otherwise identical market-B request receives its independently configured rule outcome.
P258.theoretical_adverse_test: An unknown jurisdiction remains unresolved. Simultaneous applicable permit/prohibit rules without an approved precedence produce a conflict. Passing an evidence checklist alone cannot establish product eligibility.

P259.title: agreement versions and structured terms -> party- and version-bound checks -> negotiation and execution register

P259.required_implementation_and_evidence: Archive the permitted agreement test corpus, approve the term schema, implement amendment and signature bindings, and test changed bytes, wrong parties, missing exceptions, and revoked authority.

P260.title: member configurations and shared controls -> constrained commonality analysis -> variation and lead-owner register

P260.new_capability: Z3 valid-configuration enumeration + clingo commonality + SHACL ownership coverage

P260.theoretical_adverse_test: Two equally eligible leads produce an unresolved owner rather than a lexicographic winner. Removing a scope dimension cannot collapse conflicting requirements into a false common control. An impossible member/product pair is rejected before evaluation.

P262.title: typed decision envelopes -> strict canonical bytes -> interoperable signatures and semantic fingerprints
P262.reuses: P17 hashes; P51 canonical packages; P195 Unicode mapping; P247 signatures
P262.new_capability: rfc8785 canonicalization + strict JSON decoding + cross-implementation test vectors
P262.contract: Sorted keys from json.dumps do not establish RFC 8785 conformance. Unicode normalization is a separate transformation and cannot silently change signed strings. Decimal strings need an explicit scale/value contract; source-byte identity and semantic-equivalence claims are separate.
P262.theoretical_positive_test: Equivalent property orderings within the supported profile produce identical canonical bytes. RFC vectors must agree byte for byte across implementations. An exact decimal represented by the approved schema remains exact after roundtrip and signature verification.
P262.theoretical_adverse_test: Duplicate allow keys are rejected before last-value-wins parsing. Unsupported large integers, NaN, unpaired surrogates, and forbidden numeric coercions fail. A Unicode ordering counterexample must expose a naive code-point sorter that differs from the required ordering.

sign and verify the canonical envelope while retaining scope and authority checks

P263.title: append-only event commitments -> inclusion and consistency checks -> auditable checkpoint with coverage limits
P263.reuses: P53 append ledger; P210 event completeness; P220 replay; P247 signed checkpoints
P263.new_capability: pymerkle inclusion/consistency + signed size/root checkpoints + explicit ingestion reconciliation
P263.contract: Inclusion proves membership in a particular committed tree. It does not prove that every required event was ingested. A self-consistent old prefix needs a trusted newer checkpoint to expose tail truncation. A valid signature does not prevent a publisher from signing conflicting histories. The library needs security review before production use.
P263.theoretical_positive_test: An authored checkpoint growing from three to five leaves verifies consistency, and each required receipt has a matching included leaf. Separate root/size checks identify exactly which checkpoint was verified.
P263.theoretical_adverse_test: Changed leaf bytes, reordered events, invalid sizes, incompatible old/new roots, or a stale checkpoint fail their respective gates. A receipt absent from the tree keeps ingestion coverage incomplete even when all supplied inclusion proofs pass.
P263.assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for stronger audit commitments, subject to independent security review and a trusted checkpoint distribution design.
P263.public_data_limit: The current bounded tests use a simple local hash-chain and sequence oracle. They do not execute pymerkle, establish Byzantine resistance, or prove receipt completeness for a live provider.

Functional noninterference covers the declared output interface; timing and resource side channels need separate analysis.

P264.theoretical_adverse_test: A global total that changes when hidden records are added fails. Embedding the full model behind a hidden panel fails. An error revealing an unauthorized case ID or a redacted source link is a disclosure defect.

P266.new_capability: Schemathesis stateful API cases + pytest custom invariants + independently modeled resource state

P266.theoretical_adverse_test: A stale version returns the declared conflict outcome and leaves resource state unchanged. Cross-tenant read/update, duplicate creates, or a success body that falsely claims the requested object must fail custom checks even if the JSON schema accepts it.

P267.title: rule compiler and tests -> semantic mutants -> counterexample-driven assurance gaps
P267.reuses: P191 grammar; P197 independent parity; P199 gates; P238 synthesis; P250 qualification
P267.new_capability: mutmut + Hypothesis + hand-specified semantic mutation operators
P267.contract: A mutation score is conditional on the selected operator set and test domain. Timeouts are not killed mutants. Equivalent mutants need a justified domain-specific classification. Shared compiler-generated expectations cannot serve as the sole independent oracle.
P267.theoretical_positive_test: An authored >=25 rule has a boundary test at 25 that kills a >25 mutation. A two-prerequisite gate has a one-present/one-missing test that kills an AND-to-OR mutation. Correct baseline behavior still passes.
P267.theoretical_adverse_test: A negation-removal, scope-widening, wrong-case evidence join, or ignored-version mutant that survives must remain an assurance gap. A skipped test cannot count as a killed mutant. Mutating both implementation and expected output together is rejected as circular evidence.
P267.assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for discovering weaknesses in otherwise passing compiler and verifier tests.
P267.public_data_limit: The bounded suite executes two hand-authored mutant comparisons only. No automatic mutmut campaign or broad semantic mutation coverage has been established.
P267.required_implementation_and_evidence: Implement a mutation catalogue tied to failure modes, run isolated baseline and mutant tests, define timeout accounting, and add independently reviewed counterexamples for survivors.

classify killed, survived, timed_out, invalid, equivalent-under-declared-domain, and untested mutations separately

P268.title: qualified implementations and fixed workloads -> accuracy-gated measurements -> reproducible scaling envelope
P268.reuses: P145 capacity limits; P229 stress scenarios; P237 drift; P250 evidence gate
P268.new_capability: pyperf multi-run benchmarks + exact workload lineage + explicit timeout/correctness accounting
P268.contract: Fast incorrect output is a failure. Solver feasible, optimal, and timed-out results cannot be compared as equivalent outcomes. P268.theoretical_adverse_test: Mixed seconds/milliseconds, excluded timeouts, changed workload semantics, an unverified solution, or missing hardware metadata block a headline comparison. An all-timeout cohort cannot report zero latency.
P268.assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for reproducible engineering performance evidence after correctness qualification.
P268.public_data_limit: The numeric reference check uses authored measurement rows. It establishes accounting mechanics only. No pyperf benchmark, scalability curve, infrastructure capacity, or private SLA has been measured.
P268.required_implementation_and_evidence: Archive workloads, qualify correctness first, pin runner and hardware settings, collect repeated measurements with all outcomes, and retain raw runs plus uncertainty and selection limits.

separate load, compile, cold execution, warm execution, serialization, and verification phases
run replicated measurements with recorded environment, seeds, thread counts, and resource limits

P269.title: sealed checkpoint and event suffix -> verified restore and reconciliation -> recoverable lifecycle state
P269.reuses: P220 exact replay; P241 workflow histories; P242 external effects; P245 migration; P263 checkpoints
P269.new_capability: Temporal replay + database snapshot recovery + source-receipt reconciliation
P269.contract: A valid snapshot hash proves only snapshot bytes. Completeness requires the full needed event suffix and trusted position. Local replay must not duplicate remote business effects. A restore cannot claim a recovery point or recovery time unless measured with explicit clocks and loss accounting.
P269.theoretical_positive_test: An authored snapshot after events 1-2 plus an overlapping replay of events 2-4 produces the same four-event state as uninterrupted execution. Existing event 2 is retained once and matching remote receipts suppress duplicate dispatch.
P269.theoretical_adverse_test: A modified snapshot, missing event 3, reused event ID with changed content, incompatible upcaster, or an unconfirmed remote effect prevents a fully reconciled recovery claim. A local successful restore does not prove remote-state recovery.

P269.public_data_limit: The bounded suite tests SQLite memory serialization/deserialization and deterministic replay only. No distributed outage, Temporal restoration, production backup, remote effect, recovery time, or recovery-point target was tested.
P269.required_implementation_and_evidence: Run isolated kill/restart and storage-loss scenarios, archive service histories and receipt inventories, validate schema migrations, and compare full state plus external effects to an uninterrupted control run.

restore the database and workflow history using the qualified version/migration path

P270.title: policy change during entity-add -> invalidated gates and scoped rework -> newly verified readiness

P270.contract: An old approval does not approve a new policy or materially changed evidence set. A completed document task does not prove configuration. Rework scope derives from semantic dependencies and newly applicable conditions, not just previous output links. Historical approvals remain historical records even when current readiness is invalidated.
P270.theoretical_positive_test: An authored version-1 case satisfies its identity requirement. Version 2 adds ownership review. The case becomes blocked; completing the added evidence still leaves the old approval stale. A new scope-matched approval plus all verified configurations produces version-2 readiness.
P270.theoretical_adverse_test: Deliver the old approval late, replay the change twice, complete the wrong entity's document, omit one configuration receipt, or crash after a remote effect. Every ordering must preserve the same safety invariant: no current activation without the current manifest, evidence, authority, and verified configuration.
P270.assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for the central evolving-onboarding use case as one composed system. The theoretical chain is coherent under the stated contracts; implementation, data completeness, authority, and all engine-boundary tests remain required.
P270.public_data_limit: No selected public dataset joins real bank policy changes, ownership, agreements, approvals, and configuration receipts for the same case. Public sources support separate mechanics. End-to-end domain validity needs an authorized, owner-approved case pack.
P270.required_implementation_and_evidence: Build all typed adapters, qualify the complete isolated chain, enumerate a bounded interleaving domain with explicit fairness, run restarts and negative tests, and bind each stage to fresh execution evidence before any promotion.

steps.step: preserve the earlier decision basis and select newly applicable rules at the declared cutoff
derive the entire new requirement manifest and its delta, including newly affected cases
invalidate only the dependent current approvals/readiness assertions, preserving historical records
plan and execute authorized outstanding work with stable episode and effect identities
reconcile exact agreement, ownership, evidence, and configuration versions at the final barrier

P271.title: source-bound contradiction -> checked irreducible subset -> smaller conflict explanation with explicit minimality status

P271.reuses: P193 scoped contradictions; P197 independent engine checks; P212 change impact
P271.new_capability: Z3 assumption-based cores + deletion reduction + independent finite-domain subset oracle
P271.contract: Irreducible means that removing any one member makes the reported subset satisfiable relative to the fixed background. It does not mean globally smallest cardinality. Background assumptions and domain bounds are part of the explanation. A timeout leaves reduction incomplete. Two different irreducible cores can be valid.
P271.theoretical_positive_test: For the authored integer domain -1 through 6, minimum q>=4 and cap q<=3 remain a conflict while distractor q>=0 is removed. Each surviving rule is required for that subset. A second fixture deliberately returns an irreducible three-rule core while another two-rule core exists, preventing a smallest-core claim.
P271.theoretical_adverse_test: Changing scope during reduction, hiding a background constraint, treating unknown as satisfiable, or labeling the first returned core globally minimum fails. A conflict that disappears only because the case inputs were changed is a different assessment.
P271.assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for readable harmonization explanations that preserve the source and the exact conflict context.
P271.public_data_limit: Public norms and authored contradictions exercise explanation mechanics. No private requirement conflict or human resolution authority is verified. The local reference checks enumerate finite cases; Z3 core extraction itself was not run.

P272.title: blocked requirement manifest -> authorized corrective actions -> least-cost repair proposal with controls protected

P272.theoretical_adverse_test: Allowing the solver to rewrite identity, ownership, jurisdiction, evidence freshness, or mandatory approval fails. Missing cost does not become zero. An unqualified reviewer, negative cost, unavailable action, or invalid plan blocks the proposed repair.

P272.required_implementation_and_evidence: Approve the action catalog and hard constraints, encode real effects and rollback limits, verify the proposal independently, and require separate authorization and observed completion for each selected action.

P273.title: finite variation dimensions -> decision diagram -> counted and explainable valid configuration space

P273.reuses: P198 rule coverage; P200 resolver; P260 member commonality
P273.new_capability: dd.autoref.BDD + explicit finite-value encoding + Z3 and exhaustive-count parity
P273.contract: A Boolean representation is only meaningful with its encoding and counted variable universe. Irrelevant but declared variables can multiply complete assignments. Projection removes dimensions deliberately. Variable ordering may change memory use; this proof does not promise polynomial size or superior performance. Untrusted pickle is excluded.
P273.theoretical_positive_test: The authored constraint a implies b has six assignments over a,b,c and three assignments over the projection a,b. A bijective rename preserves the complete assignment set after decoding. Each invalid one-hot categorical combination is excluded.
P273.theoretical_adverse_test: Dropping c while continuing to report complete configurations, counting unused bit patterns as categories, conflating absent values with false, or loading a diagram with a mismatched variable map fails. Resource exhaustion reports incomplete processing.
P273.assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for compact variation resolution, coverage accounting, and change-impact enumeration on qualified finite domains.
P273.public_data_limit: Public examples establish finite configuration mechanics. Actual banking dimensions, allowed combinations, and diagram scale require private owner-approved inputs. dd was not executed in the local suite; its count contract requires adapter tests.

P274.title: valid configuration space -> constrained interaction tests -> measured pairwise and higher-order coverage
P274.reuses: P198 coverage; P267 mutation tests; P273 configuration diagram
P274.new_capability: allpairspy.AllPairs + satisfiable-prefix filter + independent interaction-coverage enumerator
P274.contract: Pairwise coverage is a coverage property for pairs. It supplies no universal guarantee for three-way or higher interactions. A prefix containing an unknown suffix must not be rejected merely because the suffix is absent. Solver unknown leaves target validity unresolved rather than removing it from the denominator.
P274.theoretical_positive_test: The authored rows 000,011,101,110 cover all value pairs across three Boolean dimensions. A fault that occurs only at 111 remains uncovered and requires an explicit higher-order case. Under a implies b, prefix [1] has a valid completion; [1,0] does not.
P274.theoretical_adverse_test: Calling a pairwise suite complete for the whole resolver, rejecting all incomplete rows, silently excluding a valid but difficult pair, or calculating coverage only from generated rows fails. Duplicate test rows cannot increase coverage.
P274.assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for economical test generation with an honest and independently checked coverage statement.
P274.public_data_limit: No private variation registry or representative fault distribution was supplied. The bounded suite checks the pair/triple counterexample and prefix oracle; allpairspy and solver filtering were not run together.
P274.required_implementation_and_evidence: Implement the partial-row contract, independently construct valid targets, preserve high-order control cases, run actual adapters, and retain uncovered interactions and mutation survivors as open requirements.

P275.title: unresolved request dimensions -> authorized question partitions -> next evidence request without invented answers
title_roles: next evidence request without invented answers
P275.reuses: P200 unresolved manifest; P206 entitlements; P233 uncertainty; P273 finite configurations
P275.new_capability: BDD/Z3 partitioning + deterministic minimax selection + optional approved probabilistic utility
P275.contract: Question selection is a proposal to gather evidence. It cannot choose the answer that makes a case pass. Unknown answers preserve the applicable uncertainty. A minimax objective needs no invented probability distribution. Privacy, purpose, and mandatory evidence collection constrain the available questions before ranking.
P275.theoretical_positive_test: For four authored feasible cases, a permitted question splitting them 2+2 beats one splitting them 1+3 under the declared minimax objective. A question with no verifiable answer leaves all four possible cases available. Equal scores use a recorded deterministic tie rule.
P275.theoretical_adverse_test: A forbidden question is excluded even if it has the largest possible information gain. Missing priors block probability-weighted ranking. Defaulting an absent response to the most favorable class, or selecting questions from unauthorized data, fails.
P275.assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for focused intake and follow-up requests that expose the reason for each requested item.
P275.public_data_limit: Public profile and inference examples contain no private document-request permissions or cost model. The local reference tests verify authored partitions only; they establish no measured reduction in client effort.
P275.required_implementation_and_evidence: Approve the question catalog and evidence types, implement scoped access controls, verify partition conservation, and test each returned answer through the same source and freshness gates as ordinary evidence.

steps.step: remove questions outside the request purpose, audience, or information-sharing policy
partition feasible configurations by each question's verified answer classes
rank questions by an explicitly declared objective such as worst remaining set size
use expected utility only when an approved prior and answer-cost model are supplied

P276.title: typed service dependencies and uncertain failure rates -> Boolean failure model -> scenario bounds with dependence explicit
title_roles: typed service dependencies and uncertain failure rates
P276.reuses: P207 typed interfaces; P229 stress tests; P257 readiness; P273 diagrams
P276.new_capability: SymPy Boolean formulas + Fraction scenario evaluation + SciPy linear-program bounds
P276.contract: Graph reachability alone does not define system failure. Independence is an assumption that must be declared. Known marginal failure rates generally leave a range for a compound event. Exact rational reference values and floating solver results keep separate precision descriptions. Unmodeled common causes remain a model limit.
P276.theoretical_positive_test: For authored event probabilities A=0.1, B=0.2, C=0.05 and failure C OR (A AND B), independent joint enumeration gives 69/1000. With only those marginals, an eight-world linear program gives bounds [0.05,0.15]. The local SciPy result must satisfy all mass and marginal constraints.
P276.theoretical_adverse_test: Adding failure probabilities as if events were disjoint, multiplying them without an independence assumption, double-counting a shared provider, or accepting negative/inconsistent joint masses fails. A solver failure leaves bounds unresolved.
P276.assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for transparent resilience and capacity scenarios with explicit dependence uncertainty.
P276.public_data_limit: The published event logs and scheduling examples do not supply operational outage rates, causal failure independence, or complete dependency semantics. The bounded local calculation is an authored scenario, not an estimated production reliability figure.
P276.required_implementation_and_evidence: Approve the failure formula and coverage boundaries, obtain dated evidence for probabilities or label assumptions, validate solver tolerances, and compare scenarios against observed failures before any operational reliability claim.

chain.inputs: source-bound service dependency types + declared failure formula + probability assumptions

steps.step: distinguish all-required services, alternatives, and shared dependencies
compile and simplify the Boolean failure event without duplicating shared causes
evaluate joint worlds under an explicitly supplied dependence model
when only marginals are known, optimize event probability across feasible joint masses
verify probability conservation, marginal constraints, feasibility, and numerical tolerance
record scenario assumptions, lower/upper bounds, and missing failure-mode coverage

P277.title: completion model and held-out outcomes -> conformal calibration -> qualified prediction intervals with abstention
P277.reuses: P211 as-known features; P232 censored outcomes; P234 calibration; P237 drift
P277.new_capability: MAPIE split conformal regression + explicit sample splits + independent finite-sample rank oracle
P277.contract: The chosen method needs its stated assumptions. Ordinary split-conformal calibration cannot simply treat censored durations as known final targets. Marginal coverage does not establish the same coverage for every subgroup or a guarantee for one case. A time-ordered split helps prevent leakage but does not by itself establish exchangeability.
P277.theoretical_positive_test: For authored absolute residual scores 1 through 9 with alpha=0.1, the finite-sample rank is ceil(10*0.9)=9. A point estimate of 10 has radius 9 and interval [1,19]. A complete implementation must match that independent oracle for its declared simple score profile.
P277.theoretical_adverse_test: Using the training residuals as calibration evidence, overlapping case IDs, silently dropping difficult unresolved outcomes, selecting an out-of-range quantile as finite, or reporting an interval as an SLA commitment fails. Four calibration scores at alpha=0.1 do not support this finite-rank construction.
P277.assessment: CONDITIONAL_FIT for uncertainty-aware completion estimates after target, sampling, and calibration qualification.
P277.public_data_limit: The full public log was not ingested. MAPIE was not executed. The local order-statistic test verifies arithmetic and leakage guards only; empirical coverage, exchangeability, and private-program transfer remain unverified.
P277.required_implementation_and_evidence: Archive the event log and label recipe, qualify the censoring strategy, pin the MAPIE/base-model environment, run held-out coverage with subgroup diagnostics, and define drift-triggered abstention rather than automatic policy updates.

chain.inputs: as-known features + observed target definition + train/calibration/test case IDs + model assumptions

steps.step: separate training, calibration, and evaluation cases before fitting
handle unresolved or censored targets under a justified method rather than substituting elapsed time
fit the approved base predictor and compute held-out conformity scores
generate intervals with the configured coverage level and score definition
verify the finite-sample quantile and evaluate interval coverage/width on held-out cases
retain exchangeability, drift, subgroup, and data-sufficiency limitations

P278.title: four-state evidence rules -> paired Boolean rails -> cross-engine semantic checks without unknown-value collapse
title_roles: cross-engine semantic checks without unknown-value collapse
P278.reuses: P191 rule AST; P197 cross-engine parity; P199 evidence gates; P246 engine migration
P278.new_capability: SymPy paired-support algebra + Z3/clingo/clipspy adapters + complete small truth tables
P278.contract: For this declared algebra, negation swaps rails; conjunction uses (t1 AND t2, f1 OR f2); disjunction uses (t1 OR t2, f1 AND f2). Applicability and authorization remain separate dimensions. Classical simplification cannot be applied directly to a four-state proposition. The semantics must be approved before compilation.
P278.theoretical_positive_test: All four unary negations and sixteen ordered binary input pairs match the independent truth table. Double negation and the declared De Morgan identities hold. For neither, p OR NOT p remains neither. Contradictory evidence remains both and is routed under the separate decision policy.
P278.theoretical_adverse_test: Casting unknown to Python False, erasing refutation once support appears, rewriting every p OR NOT p to supported, or allowing an unsupported temporal/deontic operator through an unqualified adapter fails. Engine agreement without the independent table is insufficient.

P299.contract: Locale parsing establishes a numeric interpretation under a chosen convention. It does not validate a translation, issuer, currency, field meaning, or document authenticity. The same characters can have different values under different locales. The machine's default locale is never a silent input. Lenient and strict parsing are separate supported modes; changing one is a profile change.

The public unknown-total header remains unresolved for complete coverage. A full 200 response must not be appended to an existing partial file. A weak version validator is outside this selected profile.
